1.note: The story of Yoḥanan ha-Ḥoroni in the sukkah is Mishnah Sukkah 2:7; kept as printed.

2.he: הנה מספר מאמריהם בסדר זרעים ששים וששה
2.note: 35 halakhot + 7 midrashim + 16 fences = 58, not 66; the other orders add up. Kept as printed.

3.note: Damaged word in the print (looks like בחו); read בתהו, 'in vain'.

4.note: Print reads נמנעו ('refrained'); the sense fits poorly; perhaps a misprint for a verb like 'strove'.

5.note: Folio number hard to read (קי"ו or קי"ז); the passage is at Yevamot 116b–117a.

6.note: Mishnah number unclear in print (מ"ו or מ"ז); the elders of both Houses appear in Sukkah 2:7.

7.note: The Zealot slogan and Judah the Galilean are in Antiquities book 18 (18.1.1, 18.1.6); kept as printed.

8.note: Print blurred (OCR ממ"ו); read 2:7, the Mishnah with a dispute of the Houses.

9.note: As printed: 'Mishnah' with a halakhah number; the sailing case is in Yerushalmi Shabbat 1 (cf. footnote 4 on p. 172: 'Yerushalmi 1:8').

10.note: Printed מסלדות; Sanhedrin 69b deals with מסוללות, women who rub against one another; rendered so.

11.note: Abbreviations; ר"י may be R. Judah or R. Yose, and ריב"ב R. Yoḥanan ben Beroka or R. Judah ben Betera.

12.note: Compressed phrase; rendered as 'we do not fear that they will exude liquid [and become susceptible], since we attribute'; שתולין is unclear.

13.note: Kilayim has only nine chapters; reference kept as printed.

14.note: Print blurred; could also be מי"ב.

15.note: Chapter number blurred in the print.

16.note: Abbreviation unclear in the print; read as a reference to Hananiah ben Hezekiah who reconciled the contradictions of Ezekiel.

17.note: Talmudic idiom, 'who plastered and who beat it smooth', i.e. who would take it upon himself.
